title: partner upload threat canvas
question: Where can identity, malicious content, disclosure, denial, or privileged misuse enter a partner-upload design, and which design decision can reduce each path?
scenario: Partner document upload: A partner uploads regulated documents through an API to an internal processing service.
focalRelation: Actors send data across explicit trust changes to processes and stores; an abuse path attaches to the component, flow, boundary, or privilege it exploits; mitigation and test link back to that path.

nodes.label: Partner Actor
nodes.detail: The external partner submits a regulated document and associated identity through the approved upload interface.

nodes.label: API gateway
nodes.detail: The API gateway authenticates the partner, limits request rate and size, and validates the declared request envelope.

nodes.label: Validation Decision
nodes.detail: The validation decision applies content, identity, schema, and action rules before any internal processing.

nodes.label: Processing Service
nodes.detail: The internal service processes only an authorized document under a scoped workload identity.

nodes.label: Rejected Or Quarantined Request
nodes.detail: A failed upload stops before normal processing and moves to a bounded rejection or quarantine path.

nodes.label: Document Store
nodes.detail: The protected store accepts only the authorized processed result and records the write.

lanes.label: External actor and input
lanes.rule: The partner and submitted document begin outside the application trust boundary.

lanes.label: Boundary decisions
lanes.rule: The gateway validates identity, content, and action before processing.

lanes.label: Protected processing and data
lanes.rule: Only accepted work reaches the service and store; rejected work is quarantined.

variants.label: Scanning moves to a supplier
variants.changedFact: Scanning moves from the organization’s upload service to a supplier, and the supplier now controls signature updates.

lanes.label: External submission
lanes.rule: Partner content begins outside both the organization and supplier trust boundaries.

lanes.label: Supplier scanning boundary
lanes.rule: The supplier operates scanning and signature updates under bounded authority and assurance.

lanes.label: Organization processing boundary
lanes.rule: The organization validates the supplier result and retains its own accept-or-quarantine decision.

nodes.label: Partner document upload
nodes.detail: The partner submits regulated content that may be malformed or malicious.

nodes.label: Supplier scanning service
nodes.detail: The supplier receives content across a new trust boundary and performs malware inspection.

nodes.label: Supplier signature-update authority
nodes.detail: The supplier controls scanner signature and engine updates, creating a privileged dependency and compromise path.

nodes.label: Signed scan result
nodes.detail: The supplier returns a result whose identity, freshness, integrity, and scope require validation.

nodes.label: Organization validation gate
nodes.detail: The organization checks supplier identity, result freshness and integrity, content policy, and failure state before processing.

nodes.label: Process or quarantine decision
nodes.detail: Accepted content enters scoped processing; failed, stale, or unverifiable results enter quarantine.

states.title: The trust boundary and update authority move
states.caption: Partner content now crosses into a supplier service, and the supplier controls the scanner update path.

statuses.partner: The partner supplies untrusted regulated content.
statuses.supplier-service: The scanning function now runs outside the organization boundary.
statuses.update-feed: Supplier-controlled updates can change scanning behavior and require assurance.

states.title: Retain an internal decision gate
states.caption: Require an attributable, fresh scan result, validate it inside the organization, and quarantine content when the result or supplier control cannot be trusted.

statuses.supplier-service: The supplier operates within stated service, update, and evidence obligations.
statuses.scan-result: The result names scanner identity, signature version, time, content reference, and outcome.
statuses.internal-gate: The organization validates the supplier evidence instead of inheriting supplier trust.
statuses.process-or-quarantine: Only content with an accepted result enters scoped processing; other content is quarantined.

assumptions: Only entities and claims anchored in the canonical unit or explicitly labeled hypothetical scenario are used.
A highlighted path means the learner is inspecting that path; it does not assert the event occurred.
The current source is authoritative for facts; this treatment reorganizes presentation without changing canonical content.
The lesson teaches one bounded decision and does not claim to exhaust every jurisdiction, vendor implementation, architecture, attack, or exception.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The boundary states preserve the reviewed partner-upload actors, flows, trust boundary, concrete abuse paths, and treatment decisions. Abuse paths are revealed through authored states rather than toggles or a method selector.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Threats must attach to concrete actors, flows, components, boundaries, privileges, or assumptions. Moving scanning to a supplier changes the boundary and gives the supplier update authority that must be modeled.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: The boundary canvas adds actual control points and rejected paths, especially in the supplier variant; it enables more reasoning than a generic threat checklist.
